subjects.displayTitle: Nearness and remoteness: the distances of the heart
subjects.introduction: A person far away may be intimately present, while someone standing nearby may remain a stranger. These readings unsettle the geography of nearness and invite us to consider the orientation of the heart. Letters console those separated from a beloved presence; prayers voice the pain of distance; and philosophical passages distinguish spiritual relationship from location in space. Images of sunlight, polished surfaces, oceans, and gardens suggest a nearness shaped by receptivity, recognition, and love. The language of longing is joined to practical movement: service, good thoughts, and good deeds become ways of drawing close. Neighboring subjects extend the inquiry toward spiritual life, belief, mortality, and the meanings of heaven and hell. The Qur’an’s assurance of divine nearness to the one who prays offers a comparative reading. Together these passages ask how companionship and responsibility might deepen even when outward circumstances keep people apart.
subjects.arc: Begin with the paradox of distant presence, explore nearness beyond physical location, listen to the prayers of separation and companionship, then follow recognition and love into service and daily conduct.

subjects.displayTitle: Human capacity: difference, dignity, and development
subjects.introduction: What might change if we sought to fill our own vessel rather than measure it against another’s? These readings explore differences of capacity alongside human equality, the right to education, and the duty to treat no one with contempt. Images of gardens, mirrors, bodies, and rivers offer several ways to imagine diversity. Accounts of innate qualities and acquired character raise difficult questions about what education can accomplish and what an observer can know about another person’s possibilities. The compilation preserves historical explanations of inheritance and development, while also warning against expecting every perfection in every person. Neighboring subjects on developing capacity, divine grace, and universal recognition invite us to examine the limits of fixed judgments. Paul’s picture of a body whose members need one another supplies a comparative reading. Together these sources turn attention toward cultivation, mutual dependence, and the gifts that might emerge through patient encouragement.
subjects.arc: Begin with dignity and shared belonging, explore the meanings and limits of difference, examine education and receptivity, and return to the responsibility to cultivate gifts without contempt.

subjects.displayTitle: Prayers for firmness: strength to serve and unite
subjects.introduction: A prayer for strength may begin by admitting how easily the heart can tremble. In this compilation, firmness is sought as a gift that enables service, steadies love, and gathers a divided community. Feet on a path, rooted trees, mountains, shelters, and refreshing rain give perseverance a rich imaginative vocabulary. Many prayers arose amid opposition and breaches of the Covenant; their urgent language preserves the strain of those circumstances. Alongside these appeals, requests for humility, good character, healing, and joyful remembrance invite a fuller understanding of steadfastness. The neighboring subjects connect the prayers with the Covenant’s role in unity and with the daily practice of faithfulness. Psalm 51 offers a comparative movement from inward renewal toward helping others. Reading these prayers together invites reflection on how a person may become more dependable, compassionate, and able to serve through uncertainty and trial.
subjects.arc: Open with the repair of division and the strength to serve, hear personal and communal petitions for steadiness, attend to their historical struggles, and conclude with renewal, good character, and unity.
